title: Providing Child Car Seats in Taxis and Private Hire Cars
what_it_is: Providing Child Car Seats in Taxis and Private Hire Cars

sections.label: Child car seats in taxis
sections.summary: Young passengers of all cars must be secured in a child car seat, but taxis have no such legal requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, that is why we require young passengers of all cars to be secured in a child car seat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If your child rides a taxi today, there is no legal requirement for them to sit in a child car seat.

sections.label: Government-provided taxi child seats
sections.summary: The Government should provide two child car seats to every taxi and PHC, one for ages nine months to four and one for four and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government should provide two child car seats to every taxi and PHC currently on the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Children of different ages require different child car seats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, the first seat should be for children aged nine months to four years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The second seat should be for those aged four and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The World Health Organization states that a child car seat reduces the risk of injury by up to 90%.

sections.label: MOT on taxi street-hail
sections.summary: MOT said taxis are street-hailed and cannot afford boot space and installation trade-offs, but only about 20% of rides are street-hail today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In particular, MOT has said that taxis are street-hailed and cannot afford the trade-offs of boot space and installation time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This used to be true; but today, only about 20% of all rides are street-hail and I am sure all of us in this House will agree that a parent with kids will book a taxi rather than use street-hail.

sections.label: Setting up two car seats
sections.summary: Taxi and PHC drivers were shocked that the speaker takes one minute and 16 seconds to set up two car seats and buckle in daughters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Again, taxi and PHC drivers were shocked when I show them how I take just one minute and 16 seconds to set up the two car seats, including buckling my daughters up in them.

sections.label: Government should provide car seats
sections.summary: The proposal asks the Government to step in and provide the child car seats rather than impose costs on parents and drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Rather than impose costs on parents and taxi and PHC drivers, my proposal asks that the Government steps in to provide these child car seats.

sections.label: Spending on bus belts and PMDs
sections.summary: After a 2008 school bus accident, over $35 million was set aside to retrofit seat belts in small buses, and around $15 million is spent on PMD grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: After a boy was flung out of his school bus in a road accident in 2008, we set aside more than twice the amount – $35 million – to retrofit seat belts in small buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More recently, we are also spending around $15 million in grants and incentives to reduce the dangers from PMDs.

sections.label: Child car seats in accidents
sections.summary: In about 50% of road accidents involving children, child car seats were not used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Indeed, in about 50% of road accidents involving children, child car seats were not used.

sections.label: Hospitals supplying low-price infant car seats
sections.summary: Hospitals could provide infant car seats at a low price, with previous discussions about a subsidised seat costing as low as $99 and market options from $79.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To help parents, hospitals could provide infant car seats at a low price.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand there were previous discussions with hospitals about supplying a subsidised infant car seat costing as low as $99.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, there are options out in the market now costing as low as $79.

sections.label: Funding car seats and taxi rules
sections.summary: MediFund could cover costs for lower income families, Child Development Account use could be allowed, and Germany, California and New South Wales require child car seats in taxis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To help lower income families manage costs, this can then be covered by MediFund where needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can also consider allowing parents to use their Child Development Account to pay for this infant car seat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition, jurisdictions, such as Germany, California and New South Wales, already require the use of child car seats in taxis.

sections.label: Taxi injury-causing accidents daily
sections.summary: Taxis are involved in about three injury-causing accidents on average each day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Taxis are involved in, again, about three injury-causing accidents on average each day.

sections.label: Child restraint rule and taxi exception
sections.summary: Passengers under 1.35 metres in height must be properly secured using approved child restraints or booster seats in motor vehicles, with taxis the only exception.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As an additional measure to protect our children, we require all passengers under 1.35 metres in height to be properly secured using approved child restraints or booster seats when travelling in motor vehicles.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Taxis are the only exception to this rule.

sections.label: LTA 2019 taxi consultations
sections.summary: In 2019, LTA conducted consultations with the public, drivers, operators and other stakeholders on regulatory changes for the taxi and private hire car sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In 2019, LTA conducted consultations with the public, drivers, operators and other stakeholders on a suite of regulatory changes for the taxi and private hire car, or PHC, sector.

sections.label: Parent support for child restraints
sections.summary: Less than half of parent respondents to the public consultation supported requiring all children to be secured in child restraints or booster seats in taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Amongst parents, less than half the respondents to the public consultation supported requiring all children to be properly secured in child restraints or booster seats in taxis.

sections.label: Child seat requirement reduces capacity
sections.summary: Imposing a child seat requirement would reduce carrying capacity to four, requiring this family to take two taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: If we impose a child seat requirement, the carrying capacity will be reduced to four and this family will need to take two taxis.

sections.label: Taxi operators on diverse passengers
sections.summary: Operators said taxis must serve diverse passengers and cannot feasibly carry the full range and number of child restraints and booster seats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Operators also provided feedback that taxis are expected to meet the needs of diverse groups of passengers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: It is not feasible to expect taxis to be equipped with the full range and number of child restraints and booster seats to cater to the different age groups and number of child passengers that they may pick up.

sections.label: Family-friendly ride-hail bookings rise
sections.summary: Bookings for family-friendly ride-hail services, where parents can indicate child restraint and booster seat needs in advance, have increased significantly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: In the meantime, we have observed a significant increase in the number of bookings for family-friendly ride-hail services where parents can indicate their requirement in advance for child restraints and booster seats.

sections.label: SMRT booster seat trial and proposals
sections.summary: About 1,750 SMRT taxis each had a free booster seat but take-up was low; the Member's first and third proposals will be shared with agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For the trial, about 1,750 SMRT taxis were equipped with a booster seat each.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Although SMRT's booster seats were provided at no extra cost to the passengers, the take-up rate was still low.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We acknowledge the Member's proposals to provide one child seat and one booster seat in each taxi – his first proposal; and to work with hospitals to increase access and use of infant car seats – his third proposal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: These are new ideas which we will share with the relevant agencies and stakeholders.

sections.label: Current equilibrium and future models
sections.summary: Parents needing child restraints can book ride-hail while urgent street-hail users do not breach the law; viable models will be explored.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, we have a workable equilibrium where parents who require child restraints and booster seats can book a ride-hail trip while those that need a street-hail taxi urgently can do so without breaching the law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We will look into viable business and operational models that can provide options for those who need child restraints and booster seats while balancing diverse needs by different families.
